His father Kemal established the group's original construction business. Uzan became prominent through Star television and Telsim, before the family's Turkish companies were taken over by state authorities amid banking and debt disputes.

long_biography.plain_text:
Media entrepreneur Cem Uzan entered television with Ahmet Özal while Turkey still reserved domestic broadcasting for the state. They used studios in Germany and satellite transmission to reach Turkish viewers. Star became the country's first private television channel, offering an alternative to the state broadcaster before private broadcasting was formally permitted.

Uzan also bought İstanbulspor and financed recruitment intended to make it a major force in Turkish football. The club returned to the top division in 1995 and fielded players including Sergen Yalçın and Aykut Kocaman. He resigned as president three years later, after which the family's financial support began to diminish.
